analysis:
Documentation-only PR. docs/provider/attestation.md bumps 'Last updated' to 2026-10-21 and adds one paragraph (head lines 142-143) saying that when status/doctor reports App Attest authorizes the connection but MDM removal needs fresh coordinator readiness, the operator should keep existing profiles installed and wait for a fresh decision. It also says the serving lease can remain valid after removal readiness goes stale. docs/provider/cli-reference.md adds one bullet (head line 1274) making the same distinction for both doctor summaries. No code, policy or wire behavior changes.

The new text keeps serving authorization (A-016, T-053) separate from MDM-removal readiness (T-057). It matches the existing guidance that removal needs a coordinator decision received within the last 10 seconds, a current daemon snapshot and an unexpired authorization. It is conservative: it tells users to keep profiles, not to remove them early. It does not weaken any threat-model mitigation.

Unverified contracts: the referenced files `provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Diagnostics/ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.swift` (`summary`) and `docs/reference/provider-authorization.md` are not in the supplied evidence. I could not confirm that they exist or that the doctor and status output behaves as described. This is a documentation-accuracy question, not a security finding. A later pass could check that the link target exists and that the code matches the claim that the serving lease and removal readiness are reported as separate decisions.

No finding, no new attack surface, and no threat-model update needed.
